sentences.en: This is going to sound like a stand-up comedy bit, but I was on my way to the airport recently,
sentences.zh: 接下来的话听起来像是个单口喜剧段子，但我最近在去机场的路上，

sentences.en: and I needed the confirmation email for my flight so I could get my boarding pass.
sentences.zh: 我需要找到航班的确认邮件，这样才能拿到登机牌。

sentences.en: So I pulled out my phone, and I typed in some keywords into the search bar of the mail program.
sentences.zh: 于是我掏出手机，在邮件程序的搜索栏里输入了一些关键词。

sentences.en: I started with the airline I thought I was taking, but that search pulled up mailing list promotions and old flights.
sentences.zh: 我先是输入了我想搭乘的航空公司，但搜索结果里全是促销邮件和旧航班信息。

sentences.en: And I know if I searched long enough and hard enough, I could eventually find it.
sentences.zh: 我知道如果我花足够长的时间、足够努力地去搜，最终肯定能找到。

sentences.en: But the thing is, by now, I'm at the airport, and I just have this naive conviction that searching should be better and easier.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，当时我已经到了机场，我有一种天真的执念，觉得搜索应该更简单、更方便才对。

sentences.en: But I often come up empty.
There are days when I feel like I've control-effed up my life into oblivion,
sentences.zh: 有时候我觉得自己把生活搞得一团糟，简直到了无可救药的地步，

sentences.en: and I'll never easily find the email I need, much less old photos and documents on my hard drive.
sentences.zh: 我根本没法轻易找到需要的邮件，更别提硬盘里的旧照片和文档了。

sentences.en: The good news is, I'm not alone.
Adam Rogers feels this particular pain, too.
sentences.zh: 亚当·罗杰斯也有同样的痛苦。

sentences.en: You know, you think email's a problem, so try to find a Slack you once wrote.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你以为邮件是个问题，那试着找找你以前写过的一条Slack消息吧。

sentences.en: You know, try to find a tweet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，试着找一条推文。

sentences.en: Try to search for a photo on Flickr, Instagram, PintereSt.
Adam's a senior tech correspondent at Insider.
sentences.zh: 亚当是《内幕》杂志的资深科技记者。

sentences.en: He's been thinking and writing about what's known in the industry as search.
sentences.zh: 他一直在思考和撰写关于业内所谓“搜索”的内容。

sentences.en: For the last decade, people have been grumbling about not being able to find things online,
sentences.zh: 过去十年里，人们一直在抱怨无法在网上找到东西，

sentences.en: both in our private data and on the public web.
sentences.zh: 无论是我们私人的数据，还是公共网络上的信息。

sentences.en: I would say to people, I think search sucks.
sentences.zh: 我会对人们说，我觉得搜索烂透了。

sentences.en: And other people would say, oh my god, it really does.
sentences.zh: 而其他人会说，天哪，确实如此。

sentences.en: For Adam, the stakes for this go beyond me not being able to find that one email.
sentences.zh: 对亚当来说，这件事的严重性远不止我找不到那一封邮件那么简单。

sentences.en: I will tell you, I'll tell you a personal story.
sentences.zh: 我来告诉你，我给你讲个私人的故事。

sentences.en: That is one of the ways that I started to think about this.
sentences.zh: 这就是我开始思考这个问题的方式之一。

sentences.en: My grandmother was a professor of library science at UC Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 我祖母曾是加州大学伯克利分校的图书馆学教授。

sentences.en: When Adam's grandmother was alive, she lived in a small apartment.
sentences.zh: 亚当的祖母在世时，住在一间小公寓里。

sentences.en: Every wall was filled with rows and rows of books.
sentences.zh: 每一面墙都摆满了书，一排又一排。
那些书整理得井井有条。

sentences.en: The books held all the knowledge that Adam's grandmother wanted to access.
sentences.zh: 这些书里包含了亚当祖母想要获取的所有知识。

sentences.en: It was arranged by topic and author, complete with important search tools.
sentences.zh: 它们按主题和作者排列，还配有重要的搜索工具。

sentences.en: Notes and tabs stuck into all the various volumes that she could reference
sentences.zh: 各种卷册里都夹着笔记和标签，方便她查阅，

sentences.en: when looking to pull up some tidbit of information.
sentences.zh: 当她想提取某条信息时就能派上用场。

sentences.en: Adam was charmed by the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 亚当被这一切深深吸引。

sentences.en: But, as she got older and was a little bit less coherent, she didn't remember stuff as well.
sentences.zh: 但随着她年纪渐长，思维变得没那么清晰，她记性也不如从前了。

sentences.en: And the notes became less and less coherent.
sentences.zh: 那些笔记也变得越来越语无伦次。

sentences.en: Adam's grandmother had built a working search function.
sentences.zh: 亚当的祖母建立了一套行之有效的搜索功能。

sentences.en: All the same millions of pages of information were still there, lining the walls.
sentences.zh: 那数百万页的信息依然在那里，排列在墙上。

sentences.en: But she couldn't access this archive of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但她已经无法访问这个知识档案库了。

sentences.en: According to Adam, the same thing could be happening when we search for anything on our computers.
sentences.zh: 亚当认为，当我们搜索电脑里的任何东西时，可能正在发生同样的事情。

sentences.en: More and more, we outsource our information, our personal information, and our autobiographical memories.
sentences.zh: 我们越来越多地将信息、个人信息以及自传式记忆外包出去。

sentences.en: We outsource that more and more to digital media now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在越来越多地将这些外包给数字媒体。

sentences.en: Not just the sum total of human knowledge, but also our own photos, emails, and memories stored in the cloud.
sentences.zh: 不仅是人类知识的总和，还有我们自己的照片、邮件和存储在云端的记忆。

sentences.en: As we put more and more of that somewhere else besides our own heads,
sentences.zh: 当我们把越来越多的东西放在大脑之外的地方时，

sentences.en: search becomes more and more of an existential crisis,
sentences.zh: 搜索就越来越演变成一场生存危机，

sentences.en: not just an annoying thing where I can't find the email with my confirmation number in it.
sentences.zh: 而不仅仅是我找不到确认号码邮件那种烦心事。

sentences.en: We begin to potentially literally forget ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们开始可能真的会遗忘自我。

sentences.en: Our ability to search and retrieve information at our whim
sentences.zh: 我们随心所欲搜索和检索信息的能力，

sentences.en: feels like one of the most important developments of the digital age.
sentences.zh: 感觉像是数字时代最重要的发展之一。

sentences.en: So how do we get to a point where it feels like search is failing us?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们是如何走到这一步，觉得搜索正在辜负我们的呢？

sentences.en: And how do we fix it before it's too late?
sentences.zh: 我们又该如何在为时已晚之前修复它？

sentences.en: Today, the word search sort of feels synonymous with the word Google.
sentences.zh: 如今，“搜索”这个词听起来几乎成了“谷歌”的同义词。

sentences.en: But I think it's actually one of the oldest design problems in the world.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这实际上是世界上最古老的设计问题之一。

sentences.en: From the time humans started writing stuff down,
sentences.zh: 从人类开始记录事物的那一刻起，

sentences.en: the struggle has been how to organize it all so that its contents wouldn't be lost in the stacks.
sentences.zh: 斗争就在于如何组织这一切，以免内容在书堆中丢失。

sentences.en: Search has always been an attempt to fix that problem.
sentences.zh: 搜索一直都是为了解决这个问题而进行的尝试。

sentences.en: I think for our purposes here, it does make a lot of sense to think of search as a designed experience.
sentences.zh: 我认为就我们目前的目的而言，将搜索视为一种设计好的体验是非常合理的。

sentences.en: It wasn't just walking into a library and wandering around.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是走进图书馆四处闲逛。

sentences.en: Ever since, you know, the priests who ran the libraries at Alexandria knew which scrolls went in which cubbyhole,
sentences.zh: 从亚历山大图书馆的管理员知道哪卷书放在哪个格子里开始，

sentences.en: or however they did it, and leading up through the Dewey Decimal System or Library of Congress numbers,
sentences.zh: 无论他们是怎么做的，一直到杜威十进制分类法或国会图书馆编号系统，

sentences.en: These things are what makes search possible.
sentences.zh: 这些东西正是使搜索成为可能的原因。

sentences.en: Long before we could search for things online, Google was essentially a person, a reference librarian.
sentences.zh: 在我们可以上网搜索之前，谷歌本质上是一个人，一个参考咨询馆员。

sentences.en: If you wanted to find something on, say, growing vegetables,
sentences.zh: 如果你想找关于种植蔬菜的信息，

sentences.en: you could go to the gardening or farming sections of the library.
sentences.zh: 你可以去图书馆的园艺或农业区。

sentences.en: But in the thousands of books in that huge section, you'd quickly get overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 但在那个庞大区域的数千本书中，你很快就会感到不知所措。

sentences.en: That's where reference librarians and archivists come in.
sentences.zh: 这就是参考咨询馆员和档案管理员发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: They take your topic and help you narrow it down even further,
sentences.zh: 他们会根据你的主题帮你进一步缩小范围，

sentences.en: applying their own nuanced knowledge and specialized training
sentences.zh: 运用他们细致入微的知识和专业训练，

sentences.en: to help you search better and find exactly what you're looking for.
sentences.zh: 帮助你更好地搜索，找到你真正想要的东西。

sentences.en: That's how search operated for centuries.
sentences.zh: 这就是几个世纪以来搜索的运作方式。

sentences.en: By topic, mediated by human-to-human interaction.
sentences.zh: 按主题分类，通过人与人的互动来调解。

sentences.en: But eventually, this easy flow of search hit a snag.
sentences.zh: 但最终，这种顺畅的搜索流程遇到了障碍。

sentences.en: In the mid-1940s, the snag was highlighted by an American engineer named Van-Iver Bush.
sentences.zh: 20世纪40年代中期，一位名叫万尼瓦尔·布什的美国工程师指出了这个障碍。

sentences.en: At the time, Van-Iver was convinced
that problems with search were hindering human progress.
sentences.zh: 搜索方面的问题正在阻碍人类的进步。

sentences.en: He pointed to Mendel's ideas on genetics, for example.

sentences.en: These ideas were lost for an entire generation, he said,

sentences.en: because they were buried in the avalanche of newer research.
sentences.zh: 因为它们被淹没在海量的新研究中。

sentences.en: There was no efficient way for people to parse through all that information.
sentences.zh: 人们没有有效的方法来解析所有这些信息。

sentences.en: But Van-Iver was a big believer in the potential of machines.
sentences.zh: 但万尼瓦尔非常相信机器的潜力。

sentences.zh: 那是因为你真的在依赖人类的知识和投票，以及我们自 Web 2.0 出现以来就一直依赖的各种事物。
但我的问题是，你知道，你可以在 Reddit 的搜索栏里输入搜索内容。
所以你为什么要用谷歌去搜索 Reddit？
我是说，我试过。相信我，我试过很多次了。
但 Reddit 的内置搜索，在我看来，简直是一团糟。
它确实提供了各种搜索方式。
所以它看起来好像很高级。
比如你可以搜索单个版块内的内容。
你也可以按帖子的发布时间或投票数对结果进行排序。
但归根结底，可搜索性从来都不是该公司的重点。
当你真正尝试搜索该网站时，这一点就很明显了。
所以通过使用谷歌，你将这个强大的搜索引擎与极其丰富的个人知识库结合在了一起，对吧？
